excess_tax_basis_component.validation: 71 Hong Kong component/calculation/reconciliation tests passed10.40s; exact historical example, below/at/above credit limit, decimal conservation and invalid input boundaries covered.
excess_tax_basis_component.authority: Archived Cap112 Section50(3),(5),(6) and IRD DIPN44 paragraph131 Example5 notes1/2. Official DIPN44 URL reopened2026-11-22; document dated2008, historical16percent rate used only as a regression fixture.
excess_tax_basis_component.formula: For established statutory credit rate r, source income I before foreign-tax deduction, and eligible foreign tax F: C=min(F,r*(I-F)/(1-r)); deduction=F-C; reconciled income=I-deduction. Exact fractions retained before assessment rounding.
excess_tax_basis_component.limits: Requires verified rate and deduction eligibility,0<=r<1 and F<=I. Does not derive current-year/two-tier average rates, gross-ups, losses, annual reduction ordering or final assessment. Annual workflow remains pending.

validation: 53 tests passed in9.40s across new FSIE source-credit component, existing ordinary Hong Kong calculations and profits reconciliation; includes original-source hash verification. No saved annual/API/UI acceptance claimed.
findings: Taxable FSIE receipts of a Hong Kong resident MNE may receive same-income credit capped by paid similar foreign tax and Hong Kong tax on that income.
CDTA tax claims and non-CDTA unilateral claims follow distinct routes. Ineligible bilateral direct tax is not automatically unilateral tax.
Dividend underlying profits tax not allowed bilaterally can qualify unilaterally when the MNE holds at least10percent equity at distribution. Never count the same underlying tax in both claims.
Exempt income receives no FSIE credit. A nonresident MNE may have an expense deduction route, which this credit component does not implement.
